title: Metals and Non-metals
seo_title: Grade 5 Natural Sciences and Technology: Metals and Non-metals Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 5 Natural Sciences and Technology: Metals and non-metals; uses of metals
standard_text: Metals are shiny, hard, strong, can be bent and are good conductors of heat and electricity; non-metals are often dull and are poor conductors. Metals are used for their properties, and they can rust. Materials can be processed to change their properties. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences and Technology, Grade 5, Matter and Materials: Metals and non-metals; uses of metals)
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 Natural Sciences and Technology worksheets (CAPS): properties of metals and non-metals, uses of metals, rusting, and processing materials. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Metals are shiny and conduct heat and electricity.
key_sub: Iron rusts when it gets wet in air.
body_html:
How to think about it

Metals such as iron, copper and aluminium are shiny when polished, strong, can be bent or hammered into shape, and conduct heat and electricity. Non-metal materials such as wood, plastic, rubber and glass are poor conductors (insulators).

We choose metals for their properties: copper for electrical wires, aluminium for cooldrink cans, steel for bridges. Iron and steel rust when they touch water and air; paint, oil and galvanising protect them. Processing (mixing, heating, cooling, drying) changes materials, for example clay into bricks.

Example

Why are pot handles made of plastic or wood?

They should not get hot.

Answer: they are poor conductors of heat

Example

What two things make iron rust?

A bicycle left in the rain

Answer: water and air (oxygen)

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all metals are magnetic.
  • Thinking plastic conducts electricity.
  • Thinking rust is a kind of paint.
